name: Templar
body:
In the religious orders of the world, there are the priests and clerics which are the head and face of the religion.

There are the holy warriors and warpriests which are the sword arms of the faith. Then, there are templar, the shields of the faith, tasked with protection of the temples, the religion, clergy and adherents to their faith.

Alignment: A templar’s alignment must be within one step of their deity. This modifies the alignment restriction.

Class Skills: A templar gains Knowledge (religion), Knowledge (planes) and Spellcraft as class skills but removes Acrobatics, Bluff and Survival from their class skills. This modifies class skills.

Divine Code: A Templar must adhere to the tenants of their faith and keep their normal religious holidays and times of prayer. If the templar does not maintain their faith or adhere to their deity’s tenets, they lose a point of Mettle and their maximum Mettle Pool is reduced by one until 24 hours have passed for each time they have broken this code. These effects are cumulative. This replaces code of honor.

Protect the Faithful (Su)

At 1st level, a templar can call upon the powers of their faith to defend themselves and their allies. This ability functions as the paladin ability smite evil except that the target is not restricted by alignment, the usage of this ability costs 1 Mettle and the templar gains no bonuses to attack or damage.

Instead, any attacks made by the target against allies within 10 feet of the templar deal half damage. Attacks against the templar deal full damage but the templar gains a deflection bonus to their AC equal to their Charisma bonus (if any) against attacks by the target.

This bonus increases by +1 for every four templar levels to a maximum of +5 at 20th level. The radius of the effect increases to 20 feet at 12th level.

This ability replaces test of valor.

Ecclesiastical Training (Ex)

The templar’s training includes the study of religions and the visitors to their temples. At 2nd level, the templar better applies this knowledge. The templar gains a bonus equal to 1/2 their vanguard class levels on Diplomacy, Knowledge (religion), and Sense Motive checks. Additionally, a templar automatically succeeds on any Knowledge check to recall knowledge about their faith.

This ability replaces aristocratic training.

Hands of the Faithful (Su)

At 2nd level, a templar can channel their faith through a touch. If they are good-aligned they gain lay on hands as the paladin ability except that it uses 1 point of Mettle to use. If the templar is evil-aligned, they gain touch of corruption as the antipaladin ability except that it uses 1 point of Mettle to use. If the templar is neutral-aligned they must choose between lay on hands or touch of corruption effects. Once that choice is made it may not be changed. Additionally, at 3rd level and every 3 levels thereafter, they gain mercies (as a paladin) if they have the lay on hands effect or cruelties (as the antipaladin) if they have the touch of corruption effect.

This ability replaces weapons of the defender.

Deific Shield (Su)

At 4th level, the templar channels the power of their faith into their shield. All allies adjacent to the templar gain a shield bonus equal to the templar’s own shield bonus, including all ability and enhancement bonuses. This bonus will not stack with the ally’s own shield bonus. To create this effect, the templar spends one point of Mettle and lasts for a number of rounds equal to 3 + the templar’s Charisma bonus (if any).

At 7th level, the radius of protection extends to 10 feet.

At 12th level, the radius extends further to 20 feet.

This ability replaces behind me, press the advantage and improved press the advantage.

Spellcasting

At 4th level, the templar gains the ability to cast divine spells. This ability acts as the paladin ability, including the progression of the spells per day except the templar uses the cleric spell list. The templar uses Charisma as the spellcasting ability score and to determine bonus spells.

This ability replaces trial by combat, armor training, bulwark, and second skin.

Domain Spells

At 4th level, the templar also channels the magic of their faith. When praying for their spells per day, the templar selects a domain available to their deity or faith. The spells for the levels available to the templar are automatically prepared and do not count against the normal spell progression. Additionally, the templar may spontaneously convert their prepared spells for the spells of the chosen domain.

This ability replaces uncanny dodge and changes improved uncanny dodge to uncanny dodge.

Ex-templars

If a templar violates their religious code or abandons their deity, they lose their deity given abilities (spells, domains, deific shield, hands of the faithful, and protect the faithful). They must seek atonement as the paladin must to regain their abilities.
